checks.claim: C1 Source/method fidelity and covariance range
checks.reason: The text extraction and the page images agree for every cited CLO item. These are: the periodic massive wave model (1.1)-(1.8) on pp.2-3, diagonal Phi (1.22), the HS norm (1.23), and Theorem 1.4 with sigma>max(-s,s-1) (1.24) on p.8; the interaction representation and driver (1.26)-(1.34) on pp.9-10; the four entries (4.4), Proposition 4.1 and (4.8)-(4.10) on pp.44-45; and Proposition 6.1 plus the proof of Theorem 1.4, where (4.8) with s0=s is equivalent to (1.24), on pp.63-64. With |phi_n|^2 ~ |n|^(alpha-d), (1.23) is finite iff 2sigma+alpha<0. Over s, max(-s,s-1) has minimum -1/2, at s=1/2. So the two conditions can hold together only if alpha<1. sigma=-(1+alpha)/4 gives -1/2<sigma and 2sigma+alpha=(alpha-1)/2<0. For d1 white, sigma must be below -1/2, which contradicts sigma>-1/2 for every s. At equality each dyadic annulus contributes a constant N^(2sigma+alpha-d)N^d, so the sum diverges. The note claims only that the tail inequalities are compatible. It explicitly declines an all-method no-go and a periodic/whole-line covariance identity, and it transfers nothing about normalization. The custody PDF hash c800120... matches the manifest member. In d1, the full original class (density c|q|^(alpha-1), from the accepted phase note §4) reduces to Riesz 0<alpha<1 or white alpha=1.

checks.claim: C2 Physical-mask Hilbert bound (2.1)-(2.4), scaling, white case, time tensoring, b=1/2 counterexample
checks.reason: (2.1) uses -2b=alpha-1. The conjugated kernel is |zetahat(q-k)||q|^-b|k|^b. With weight p=|q|^-b, the row integral equals ||zetahat||_1 p(q), and the column integral reduces exactly to (2.4). Both match schur_row and schur_column. I checked (2.4) independently. For |k|<=2, the singular part is integrable because 2b<1, and Schwartz decay handles the tail. For |k|>2 and |q|>=|k|/2 the bound is C|k|^-2b. For |q|<|k|/2, |q-k|>=|k|/2 gives C|k|^-2 * C|k|^(1-2b). Times |k|^2b everything stays bounded. The weighted-Schur Cauchy-Schwarz argument gives operator norm at most sqrt(C1C2); density extends it. For zetahat_R(q)=R zetahat(Rq), the substitution z=Rq, y=Rk cancels every power of R in the homogeneous norm and leaves the L1 norm unchanged (schur_rescale is the k-factor identity). For white noise the multiplier is an L2 contraction. The space-time norm is a tensor of the positive temporal spectral density c|tau|^(a-1) with the spatial weight, so applying the spatial bound for a.e. tau and integrating is valid. For b=1/2 with f=zeta'': fhat=O(q^2) gives a finite |q|^-1 norm, while (zeta f)hat(0) is proportional to -int(zeta')^2, which is nonzero. Since zeta f is Schwartz, its |q|^-1 norm is infinite. This lies outside alpha>0 and is not a no-go for the target.

Test convergence comes from the accepted source limit at zeta_R f. Every HS(E) ONB coordinate of chi_j[M_R(t)-M_R(s)] is W(zeta_R f_kl), where f_kl is the deterministic test of the unmasked coordinate. So E||.||_HS^2 <= C^2 E||chi_j[M(t)-M(s)]||_HS^2. The generic common-Gaussian criterion of the accepted driver note §5-6 then gives (3.2)/(3.3). Support: wave propagation of speed 1 on each side gives input-output radius 2u<=2T. Injection only in supp zeta_R, contained in [-2R,2R], gives output in [-2R-T,2R+T]. An input supported outside that interval has S(u)v vanishing on [-2R,2R], so zeta_R S(u)v=0. checks.reason: Completeness: localized limits w_j agree on overlaps, because compact multipliers are bounded on E. v=sum rho_l w_l is locally finite, and chi_j v=lim chi_j v_n because rho_l chi_l=rho_l. The Cauchy bound then gives sup-norm convergence. Global E embeds via translates of one multiplier, and E-density of compact smooth phases gives membership in F. Separability follows from separability of E plus the two constants. (4.2) uses finitely many l with |l-j|<=B+2. Finite propagation gives chi_j S(t)v=chi_j S(t)psi_j v, so S(t) is bounded on E_uloc uniformly for |t|<=T. Massless constants evolve as (c1+tc2,c2). Strong continuity holds on the generating set and extends to F through the uniform bound. Operator-norm continuity is explicitly not claimed.

The kappa_R definition is independent of kappa_R: (kappa-kappa')v is compactly supported outside the injection interval, so it lies in global E and is annihilated. Constants are therefore handled without assuming global E is dense in F. The output is compactly supported local E, so it lies in F. For |i|<=2R+T+4, ||chi_i[.]v||_E <= ||chi_i[.]||_HS C_B ||v||_uloc; the maximum over a finite set commutes with the Holder supremum, giving (4.4) with C_T independent of R. Using max^p <= sum^p over at most C_T R cells gives (4.5) with R^(1/p). (4.6) follows from the finite maximum of differences together with (3.3). The operator M(t)v=sum_i rho_i chi_i M(t) psi_i v is continuous and linear in the finite family of separable little-Holder HS paths, so strong measurability transfers. The construction is linear, so it applies to raw/cutoff differences on the same coupling.

In the interaction picture u=S(t)u~ with dM=S(-u)B(dW)S(u), so P(t,s)=S(t)U(t,s)S(-s), and the composition law telescopes. Joint strong continuity follows from strong continuity of S and norm continuity of U. Multiplication by W^(1,infinity) functions is bounded on H^(1/2) by interpolation and on H^(-1/2) by duality, uniformly on local phases. For v in F: B(h kappa_L) maps into compact global E. B(c) maps compact smooth data to compact smooth data, sends (1,0) to (0,c) and (0,1) to 0, so it preserves F by boundedness. By (5.6), B(h0(1-kappa_L))->0 in operator norm uniformly in t, and (0,h0) lies in F. The admissible class is a closed subspace, so t->B(h(t)) is strongly measurable in B(F). Combined with strong continuity of S, the integral (5.5) is F-valued for each v and Lipschitz in B(F) with C_T sup||h||_W1inf. Stability constants depend only on the norm bound. checks.claim: C9 Positive-width solution, Riemann sums, causality, passage to raw
checks.reason: Under the Laplace truncation consistent with the accepted K_eta scaling, K_eta(0)-K_eta(h) <= c h int_0^(1/eta) lambda^a dlambda = O(h). The heat filter gives all spatial spectral moments, and alpha>0 makes q=0 integrable. Gaussian Kolmogorov then gives joint continuity of the masked potential and its x-derivative, so it is bounded on [0,T]xR. The primitive is Lipschitz. Young Riemann sums converge to the Bochner strong integral by uniform continuity of the solution, so the integral equations coincide and Gronwall gives uniqueness. Speed 1 and local coefficient dependence come from Duhamel/Picard support (radius t-s), not from the 2T interaction kernels. They pass to the raw masked flow through a.s. subsequential operator convergence, and compact-test pairings are continuous on F. Only countably many masks, data, tests and times are used.

With wave kernel 1/2 1_{|x|<t}, the nth Picard term is bounded by (|g|M)^n t^(2n)/(2n)!, since int G(r,y)dy=r. So the pathwise series converges on compact cones. The literal L:vertex-crude bound q_n(t)=e^(theta0 t)C^(n/2)t^n/sqrt(n!) holds uniformly in all widths, so sum |g|^n q_n<infinity and pathwise and L2 sums agree. L:joint-fixed-order gives convergence of every finite prefix, and the uniform tails give convergence of the full solution; this is not substituted by summability of the canonical tails alone. Spatial stationarity of the common family makes the L2 error independent of x. The average error is at most ||phi||_1 times that error, with positive-width Fubini. The left side converges through Lp operator convergence and the bounded compact-test functional on F. zeta_R=1 on supp phi+[-t,t] covers the backward cone. Uniqueness of limits gives (6.1). No point evaluation on H^(1/2) and no positivity of samples is used; the averaged-to-point inequality (M) is the consumer.

Pairing delta^(a/2)W(delta u) with tests reproduces the raw law. delta^2V_tt=V_xx+sqrt(delta)WV becomes V_uu=V_xx+delta^((1-a)/2)W_m^delta V, with phase (V,delta V_t). Temporal cutoff eta->eta/delta and spatial widths are unchanged. There are (2c/delta+5) cells times about 1/delta blocks, at most C_c delta^-2 indices. A finite maximum, with box_scale and box_margin, gives (7.2). By (4.4), on {g Z<=eps<=1} the drivers are within C eps of A_hm with norm at most K+C. (5.3) with S bounded gives (7.3). For q>=p0>4/(1-a), delta^((1-a)/2-2/q)<=1 gives (7.4) with C sqrt(q) uniform in delta and rho, hence a uniform square-exponential moment and uniform moments through (5.2). Combined with convergence in probability this gives every finite Lp. Uniformity is stated as a supremum of individual bounds. Concatenation is at fixed delta. Closeness of the full product, spectral growth and limit interchange are explicitly not inferred.
